Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one six-sprite expansion atlas for Lost Shrine's modest tutorial village. Attached sheet is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: exactly match its simple chunky pixel shapes, muted pastoral colors and restrained detail. Do not repeat its objects.
Make a transparent landscape sheet in EXACTLY THREE COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, generous empty transparent gutters, equal cells, no labels.
Top left: low loose clump of THREE widely spaced bent meadow grass blades, asymmetrical, not bushy. Top middle: TWO small split firewood logs lying together horizontally, broad pale cut faces and dark brown bark. Top right: small low wooden bucket, dark open elliptical mouth, one simple thin curved handle, two wooden tones, no metallic highlights.
Bottom left: squat tied grain sack, straw-colored cloth, simple pinched neck and two coarse creases, no writing.
Bottom middle: flat irregular horizontal oval of lightly worn pale dirt with two subtle shoe scuffs, sparse little edge fragments, a shallow footprint of repeated standing for throwing practice. No objects, no border, no shadow. No dark deep holes. No grass surround.
Bottom right: modest UNLIT bonfire site: ring of six or seven chunky small gray-green stones seen from above/front with TWO crossed brown logs resting flat inside. No flame, no glowing embers, no smoke, no effects. A humble reusable resting-site prop.
Native design sizes: grass 16x16; split logs 32x16; bucket 16x16; sack16x16; worn ground32x16; fire ring32x32 (actual low oval about26x20). Draw at enlarged pixel scale with hard square pixel edges; objects must remain legible at these tiny resolutions. No fine stippling, gradients, extra ornaments or detailed texture. Two or three flat tones per material. Everyday cozy village, not high fantasy.
Only these color families: greens #60724D #8B9B5E #BECA82; wood #543F36 #826047 #B58C61; straw #DFC291; pale cloth #F1DEB0; stones #77766A #B2AE91. Worn dirt #B58C61 #DFC291 with very restrained darker marks. No black outlines, cyan, gold sparkle or white.
Genuine transparent background. No ground patches except the requested worn-earth sprite itself. No cast shadows or scene lighting. Exactly six distinct isolated sprites with no overlaps, text, guides, grid or borders.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one six-sprite decoration sample atlas for Lost Shrine, a cozy top-down 16-pixel-tile village game.
The attached image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its chunky simple pixel shapes, warm muted pastel palette, top-down/front readable view. Create new tiny ground decorations, much smaller and simpler than its environment props.
Composition: transparent background, landscape atlas, exactly THREE columns and TWO rows, six separate objects with very generous transparent gutters. No labels.
Top row left: three little cream meadow flowers on short muted green stems, asymmetric cluster. Top middle: one fan of five broad simple grass blades. Top right: sparse horizontal scatter of five fallen leaves in muted olive, straw and clay.
Bottom row left: one low flat weathered stone with a shallow simple circle-and-cross sunwheel carving visible on top, mundane old carving, NOT a standing pillar. Bottom middle: small squat terracotta jar with open dark mouth, no handles. Bottom right: sparse horizontal cluster of three split wood chips and a little splinter.
Pixel art: shapes must read on tiny native canvases of 16x16 pixels (flowers, tuft, stone, jar) or 32x16 pixels (leaves, wood chips). Show these pixel shapes enlarged with hard square edges. Only two or three flat tones per material. Sparse texture, no fine stippling. Stone low and flat; grass short; flowers delicate but chunky. Leaves and wood are individual loose bits, not piles.
Exact palette family: greens #60724D #8B9B5E #BECA82; timber #543F36 #826047 #B58C61; straw #DFC291; clay #794A41 #B86F50 #D99A67; cream #F1DEB0; stone #77766A #B2AE91. Flower petals cream with tiny straw centers. No saturated gold, cyan or magical accents.
No ground patches, no cast shadows, no gradients, no glow, no lighting effects, no thick black outlines, no painted background, no text, no border. Genuine transparent alpha around each object. Consistent restrained fidelity across all six sprites.

Production sprite sheet for The Lost Shrine, cozy top-down 2D RPG. Reference image is the APPROVED STYLE: match its simple blocky silhouettes, large quiet flat color areas, sparse detail, chunky native pixels, cream plaster, warm wood, soft green and terracotta. Use 2-3 FLAT tones per material. Orthographic RPG view with front faces visible, not isometric. Actual low-resolution pixel design enlarged nearest-neighbor: every pixel block about 8-12 output pixels, no tiny detail. No gradients, antialiasing, fine texture, realistic shading, individual leaves, noisy masonry, glossy bevels, shadows on the ground, ground patches, labels or text. Genuinely transparent background. Swatches ONLY foliage #384B3C #60724D #8B9B5E #BECA82; timber #543F36 #826047 #B58C61 #DFC291; roof #794A41 #B86F50 #D99A67; plaster #F1DEB0; stone #77766A #B2AE91. Keep generous transparent gutters so every object can be extracted separately. Design for small 16px tile units. Create ONE complete dilapidated stone bridge sprite for crossing a river LEFT TO RIGHT on screen. Top-down RPG view: long rectangular WALKABLE STONE DECK from left edge to right edge, with low stone parapets along TOP and BOTTOM edges, four modest end piers, some missing/chipped parapet blocks and two small muted moss patches. The central walkway must be a broad uninterrupted horizontal band, at least HALF of the total bridge height, absolutely open from left to right. No arch under the bridge, no side elevation, no stairs, no tall central structures, no river or ground. The bridge is a 160x64 NATIVE PIXEL sprite shown enlarged; pixel blocks must be coarse and deliberate. Proportions about 2.5 times as wide as tall. Stonework extremely simple: deck about 5 large slabs across and 2 slabs deep, broad flat two-tone faces, not many small bricks. Use ONLY #77766A #B2AE91 for stone, #60724D #8B9B5E for moss and very sparse #DFC291 warm edges. Centered isolated on transparent background. No shadow, haze, glow or lighting. Match the reference boulder's low detail. Large 1536x1024 image, bridge occupies most image width.

Create TWO NEW pixel-art buildings for The Lost Shrine, from scratch. The attached image is a PALETTE/SIMPLICITY reference ONLY; do NOT copy its symmetrical cottage architecture.
Transparent sprite sheet. Two buildings side by side, complete and separated. Left is a compact 6:5 width/height workshop (96x80 logical pixels). Right is an 8:6 width/height longhouse (128x96 logical pixels), visibly 33% wider and20% taller than left. Same logical pixel size throughout. Output enlarged nearest-neighbor pixel art, native pixels clearly visible. Orthographic front-facing slightly top-down RPG perspective, no isometric rotation.

LEFT: a village joiner's workshop with an asymmetric red clay saltbox roof. Taller enclosed cream-plaster/timber volume at left two-thirds, lower attached roofed work bay at right third, forming a stepped roof silhouette. Tall single timber entrance offset left (center at one-third of whole width), under a short hood supported by a diagonal bracket. A single narrow high shuttered window, placed off-center above the work bay edge. The open work bay has one support post, a simple waist-high workbench built into the structure and two broad stacked timber shapes in shadow. An off-center squat stone chimney. Purposeful architecture, no loose decorative clutter. Entire footprint6x5. Actual door panel should be about36logical pixels tall and20wide: human-scaled entrance occupies nearly45% of total sprite height.

RIGHT: a broad welcoming village longhouse, clearly different architecture. Low sweeping tan/straw hipped roof with an offset short cross-gable over the RIGHT-side entrance. Left half has a RECESSED covered porch under the main roof, two simple timber posts and a long built-in bench, with a dark broad doorway/opening behind. Main tall closed door offset right, centered at five-eighths of overall building width. One paired wooden shutter opening on the far-right plaster wall, and one tiny loft vent in the off-center gable. A modest stone hearth stack at far left interrupts the silhouette. Low gray stone plinth with two broad moss patches. Do not make two windows flanking a centered door. Footprint8x6. Main door36-40logical pixels high and22wide.

VISUAL STYLE: extremely restrained, broad flat geometric pixel shapes;2 or3 SOLID colors per material, NO gradients, dithering, texture noise, lighting, glow, blurred edges, highlights around every edge or black outlines. Roof planes mostly uninterrupted, just3-4 broad seam marks. No individual thatch strands or small shingles. Timber no grain. Small-world pastel simplicity, matching reference fidelity.
EXACT palette: deep timber #543F36, wood #826047, earth #B58C61, straw #DFC291, roof shadow #794A41, red clay #B86F50, roof light #D99A67, plaster #F1DEB0, stone #77766A #B2AE91, moss #60724D #8B9B5E. Flat filled regions only. Do not add colors. Transparent background, NO ground, NO cast shadows, NO surrounding props, NO labels, NO grid. Align the two building bases, maintain relative sizes. Creative architecture through massing, setbacks and covered functional spaces, not added ornament.

Door scale refinement:
Edit only the door/facade proportions of this newly designed two-building sprite sheet; keep architecture, roof shapes, work bay, porch, palette and layout.
LEFT workshop: it is a SINGLE-STOREY building. Remove the high slit window above the entrance. Enlarge the entrance hood and move it UP to the main eave line. Make the actual door panel almost the entire height from main eave to threshold: from approximately y=450 to y=730, about280pixels tall, instead of the current140px door. Widen door panel by25%. The big door remains at the SAME horizontal center, one-third across the workshop. Preserve stepped saltbox roof and right-side roofed workbench bay unchanged. Door must fill the tall blank left wall with only short lintel space above it.
RIGHT longhouse: raise the actual door panel's top to just beneath its lintel, remove the extra blank trim space, enlarge panel height about25% and widen25%. Keep porch, bench, asymmetric cross-gable and shutter window, and lower threshold fixed.
All door panels solid simple timber planks, broad flat fills; no added detail. Same two designs, transparent background, complete unclipped shapes, no text, no new shadows or colors.

Create a MODULAR WOODEN FENCE sprite sheet, EXACTLY NINE separate pieces in a uniform THREE BY THREE grid. Match the reference fence: square posts with a small light cap, two plain brown rails. TOP ROW: vertical fence segment running UP/DOWN on screen viewed from above (two endposts, narrow depth-oriented rails); an L-shaped corner joining NORTH and EAST; an L-shaped corner joining NORTH and WEST. BOTTOM ROW: an OPEN horizontal gate, leaf swung away to the left and a VERY CLEAR transparent walk-through gap between the posts; a horizontal fence with one visibly lighter replacement rail; one single standing square wooden endpost. No grasses, ground patches, stones, foliage, ropes, flowers, labels, lighting or effects. Very clean flat pixel shapes. Genuinely transparent background. 1024x1024.

BOTTOM ROW left to right: 5 a fallen horizontal timber log with one sawn cream end and a single short branch; 6 a short chopping stump, top clearly visible with a DARK EMPTY HATCHET NOTCH, no axe, just one ring on the top; 7 simple wooden firewood rack with six large stacked cut logs; 8 a group of three small plain flat stones. Create a production sprite sheet for The Lost Shrine, a cozy top-down 2D village game. The attached image is ONLY a style reference for the existing terrain: match its extremely simple flat color fills, deliberate chunky pixel shapes and muted pastel-like palette. Do NOT reproduce its tile sheet or labels. Make ONLY FOUR isolated new objects on a genuinely transparent background: a small cream-plaster cottage with a simple muted terracotta roof and timber door/windows; a friendly broad-crowned oak; one squat gray-green boulder; one horizontal rustic two-rail wooden fence with two endposts. Orthographic top-down RPG three-quarter view, front faces visible, no isometric angle. Beautiful clear silhouettes and charming proportions. Strict low-resolution pixel art: pretend the WHOLE sheet is 128x128 native pixels enlarged exactly 8x nearest-neighbor to 1024x1024. Cottage occupies native rectangle x4..67,y4..67 (64x64) in upper left; tree occupies x76..123,y4..67 (48x64) upper right; boulder x12..43,y88..111 (32x24) lower left; fence x64..111,y88..111 (48x24) lower right. Keep ample transparent separation. Every visible pixel block should be 8x8 at output size. Use ONLY these flat opaque hex colors: foliage #60724D #8B9B5E #BECA82 with #384B3C very sparingly; timber #543F36 #826047 #B58C61; roof #794A41 #B86F50 #D99A67; plaster #F1DEB0 #DFC291; stone #77766A #B2AE91. 2-3 tones per material. Roof has broad untextured clay planes and just a FEW short tile seam marks, NOT individual shaded shingles. Oak has 5-7 large joined geometric leafy masses, NOT many tiny leaves. Boulder has two broad planes and one small chip. Timber has flat surfaces, no grain texture. Selective muted edge definition, no thick black outlines. No gradients, no antialias, no painted lighting, no drop shadows or ground shadows, no ground patch, no ambient occlusion, no noise, no dithering, no specular gloss, no flowers or additional props, no text or grid. This is deliberately simple, calm game art to match the reference's visual fidelity.
